title: Ethiopian Corn Porridge
community: Southern Ethiopia — the corn-growing lowland porridge
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Corn Porridge — maize flour cooked into a thick, stiff porridge in the genfo style, served with a well of kibbeh and berbere. The southern Ethiopian equivalent of barley genfo — corn growing in the lowlands where barley cannot.
longDesc: Corn porridge (ye-beqolo genfo) is the southern and western Ethiopian version of genfo — where the cooler highlands grow barley and teff, the warmer lowlands grow corn, and the corn genfo is made the same way. The Ethiopian technique — the well filled with kibbeh — makes this distinctly Ethiopian rather than a generic corn porridge.
steps: See ETH009 (Genfo) for the full method.
Bring water to a boil. Add salt.
Add maize flour in a stream, whisking constantly.
Cook over medium heat, stirring vigorously, 15—18 minutes until very stiff.
Mound in bowls. Press a well in the centre.
Fill with kibbeh and top with berbere.
chefTips: Corn genfo sets faster than barley — watch carefully.
The stiffness should be the same as barley genfo.
cookingScience: See ETH009 for genfo cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Corn grows in Ethiopian lowlands where highland grains cannot — it is the grain of climatic adaptation.
healthBenefits: Kibbeh adds vitamins A and D.
culturalNote: Corn genfo is the southern lowlands' answer to barley genfo — the same preparation, the same eating ritual, the same community significance, but made from what the warmer climate provides. It demonstrates how Ethiopia's food culture adapts seamlessly across its extraordinary ecological diversity.
